signals.why_registered: A historical expert-survey anchor for the feedback-loop question. It is a dated cohort view, not a current aggregate or a calibrated probability of takeoff.
signals.snapshot_rule: Import only question-level estimates with the original survey wording, denominator, aggregation rule, and survey date.

snapshot.question_text: Some people have argued the following: If AI systems do nearly all research and development, improvements in AI will accelerate the pace of technological progress, including further progress in AI. Over a short period (less than 5 years), this feedback loop could cause technological progress to become more than an order of magnitude faster. How likely do you find this argument to be broadly correct?
snapshot.canonical_match_rationale: The source question directly asks whether AI doing nearly all R&D could create a feedback loop in which AI improvements accelerate further AI progress. It is therefore a direct aggregate-belief measure for the tracker’s AI R&D feedback question, while preserving the source’s stronger tenfold-under-five-years formulation.
snapshot.cohort: AI researchers sampled from authors who published in 2022 at NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAI, JMLR, or IJCAI; the question was assigned to a randomized subset.
snapshot.sample_or_participants: 299 responses to this question, within 2,778 respondents to the October 2023 ESPAI.
snapshot.aggregate_method: Direct response-category shares among the 299 randomized-subset responses; no mean, median, or pooled forecast was calculated.
snapshot.resolution_rule: Not applicable: this is an elicited judgment about an argument, not a resolvable platform contract.
snapshot.display: 9% quite likely · 20% likely · 24% about even · 24% unlikely · 23% quite unlikely
